label: 2026-08-12 scaffold corpus, competition tie handling, FTS over-fetch, FakeEmbedder, retirement filter
note:
Raised from 0.7791 when the FTS candidate arm began over-fetching (ftsOverfetch=4). MemoryDao.searchFts orders by decayScore DESC — freshness — so the lexical pool was 'the N freshest rows sharing any word with the query', and BM25, the vectors, RRF and the reranker all re-ranked a set chosen with no relevance signal in it. Widening the window and letting BM25 select in Kotlin is worth +0.011 here.

The second arm proposed with it — vectorPoolSize cosine-ranked rows joining the pool — ships DISABLED (0) because it was measured, not argued about: 0.4837 with it on and the floor neutralised, against 0.7976 with only the over-fetch. It injects near-noise, which is what a 384-dim hash sketch produces (random unit vectors sit at |cos| ~= 1/sqrt(384) ~= 0.051). The batch that contained both scored 0.7321, so the relevance floor was partly masking the damage rather than the arm being harmless. Re-enable only with a real embedder and a re-measurement.

Raising the baseline in the same commit is the point of the gate — a future change that gives back this gain must fail rather than pass because the bar was left low. SCAFFOLD CORPUS: absolute values are meaningless (synthetic corpus, FakeEmbedder has no semantics); what this gates is regression. See docs/RETRIEVAL_EVAL.md.

2026-08-12: correctly_empty_rate corrected from 0.0 to the measured 0.5, and zero_result_rate from 0.0 to 0.05. The 0.0 was written when the relevance floor was 0.05; raising it to 0.15 changed the measured value and the baseline was never regenerated, so `the zero-result behaviour does not regress` was asserting 0.5 >= -0.005 and could not fail for the reason it is named after. With two expect-empty queries the metric moves in steps of 0.5, so at this tolerance any regression now fails. The retirement filter (memories.retiredAt IS NULL on every read path) moved no metric.
